thread:
jen: Quick sync 2: PR #734 updates the audit-log and retention docs for SDK v2. Legal flagged two things: ambiguous TTL scope and an unclear example for redaction vs pseudonymization.

carlos: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/734. I moved the old v1 snippets into a migration note but left the TTL examples as-is.

emily: Legal asked we explicitly label examples as tenant-scoped or global/admin. Otherwise customers assume global behavior.

jene: (typo) meant jen: +1 on labeling. Also, add a short CLI and SDK redact example so engineers see default behavior.

legal-ryan: Requested wording (please use verbatim on SOC2 pages): "Retention settings shown apply to the tenant indicated unless labeled 'global/admin'. Indefinite retention (subject to legal hold) may extend preservation beyond configured TTLs." Keep it exact.

carlos: ok will add that sentence under each TTL example. For snippets I'm proposing a compact pair: JS and Python tenant examples, and a global admin example.

emily: sample snippets look good. please ensure human-friendly comments ("90 days") and machine values (seconds) are present.

carlos: here's the tenant example I'll include:

```python
# tenant-scoped: set 90-day retention for tenant 'acme'
client.set_audit_retention(tenant_id='acme', ttl_seconds=90*24*3600)  # 7776000 seconds (90 days)
# Note: retention applies to the tenant's collected logs.
```

```js
// tenant-scoped: set 90-day retention for tenant 'acme'
await client.audit.setRetention({ tenantId: 'acme', ttlSeconds: 90 * 24 * 3600 }); // 90 days
// Note: retention applies to the tenant's collected logs.
```

jen: add the global example too and label it clearly: 

```bash
# global/admin: set org default retention (affects org-wide opt-ins)
redwood admin retention set --ttl 7776000
# Global settings do not override explicit tenant configs unless the tenant opts in.
```

emily: we should also show redaction behavior in an export example and note placeholders vs pseudonymization: 

```bash
# export and redact sensitive fields
redwood audits export --tenant acme --since 2026-07-01 --redact ip,email
```

And an example output snippet in docs text: 

{"timestamp":"2026-07-01T12:00:00Z","event":"login","user":"[REDACTED]","ip":"[PSEUDONYMIZED]"}

jen: add one-line parenthetical explaining the two outcomes: '(Redaction replaces values with [REDACTED]; pseudonymization replaces with reversible tokens when configured.)'

legal-ryan: also include the private deployment line exactly: 'Private deployments may follow customer-managed retention and key policies.' That helps enterprise customers.

carlos: will push updates: 1) label tenant vs global examples, 2) add legal-approved SOC2 sentence, 3) include export + output example and note on redaction/pseudonymization, 4) migration note for v1 -> v2 snippets.

docs-bot: PR #734 updated by carlos  https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/commit/az12bc :white_check_mark:

emily: quick QA: ensure link anchors for the audit-schema and retention headings didn't change. Linkcheck will catch broken anchors but please keep headings stable.

carlos: good call  will run linkcheck and adjust anchors if CI flags anything.

legal-ryan: LGTM pending CI. Minor style ask: keep compliance wording compact so it reads well on the SOC2 landing page.

jen: thanks team. merging after legal sign-off + linkcheck. closing loop. :tada:
